newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Tapie back in jail from hospital.
newsitem.headline: France's Tapie back in jail from hospital.

text.p: Bernard Tapie, the fallen French tycoon and ex-soccer boss, returned to jail on Wednesday less than 24 hours after being rushed to hospital with a mild heart problem, medical sources said on Wednesday.
They said Tapie, 54, recovered during a 19-hour stay in a coronary intensive care unit in the southern town of Aix-en-Provence.

Imprisoned nearly four months ago for fixing a soccer match and currently on trial for embezzling money from his former Marseille soccer club, he had woken up during the night complaining of chest pains and breathing difficulties.
Tapie's trial was suspended until Thursday morning, at the earliest, due to his absence. His lawyer Jean-Yves Lienard said he was willing to return to court as soon as he is discharged.
Tapie, a rags-to-riches businessman-politician, has been on trial since May 12 on charges of embezzling 100 million francs ($17.5 million) from the Marseille team.

He was jailed after the supreme court upheld his eight-month sentence for bribing players of league rival Valenciennes to give Marseille an easy game days before Marseille beat AC Milan in the 1993 European Cup final.
Nineteen other soccer figures are standing trial along with Tapie in the Marseille case, which is expected to last another two weeks.
He faces a five-year sentence if convicted on the charges of swindling, misusing corporate funds and falsifying documents between 1987 and 1993.
